solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Bite on cup-holder (5)

blocks.note: a verb for chewing noisily, as a horse does at the bit
the winner of a trophy, in short form

annotation.surface: Someone nibbling at the handle of a teacup.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cup-holder' reads as a saucer or a car's drinks slot; it is the winner holding a trophy.
annotation.definitionFit: Champ is a verb meaning to munch or bite, and short for champion, who holds the cup.

entries.clue: Encouragement for selected pupils to start being productive (4,2,6)

blocks.note: 'Come on!' is a shout of encouragement
a stream is a group of pupils selected by ability

annotation.surface: A teacher cheering on the top set to get some work done.
annotation.walkthrough: In British schools pupils are 'streamed' into classes by ability, so a stream is a set of selected pupils.
annotation.definitionFit: A new plant or oil field comes on stream when it starts producing.

entries.clue: Equally disposed resource (5)

blocks.note: as = equally, as in 'as tall as'
set = disposed or inclined, as in 'set on going'

annotation.surface: Something evenly distributed or sold off, like shared-out stock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Equally disposed' reads as one idea, evenly arranged; it splits into two separate words.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: anything of value you can draw on, from cash to a skill, counts as an asset.

entries.clue: Four cracks in each pot spread right across (9)

indicatorNotes.cracks in: the four breaks into the pot, sitting inside it

blocks.note: per = each, as in 'a pound per head'
a vase is a pot, split to take the four
IV is four in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: Cracks spreading all over a pot until it is covered.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Spread right across' looks like more of the crack description, but it is the definition; the cracks are the numeral forcing its way in.
annotation.definitionFit: Something pervasive has spread right across a whole area.

entries.clue: Musical comedy really riding on score that’s a failure (4,4)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B

blocks.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket
so = really, as in 'so good'
a jockey who is up is riding

annotation.surface: A review saying a musical show is a flop whose score is terrible.
annotation.walkthrough: The score looks like the music of the show; it is a cricket score. Duck Soup is the 1933 Marx Brothers film, full of songs.
annotation.definitionFit: Duck Soup is a Marx Brothers comedy with musical numbers.

entries.clue: Exhausted German’s no party tops (4,2)

indicatorNotes.tops: in a down clue, the party sits on top of the German word

blocks.note: a do is a party
nein is German for no

annotation.surface: A worn-out German declining to go to the top parties.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tops' reads as the best parties, or as clothing; it is a verb placing DO above NEIN.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal British idiom: after a long walk you feel done in, worn out completely.

entries.clue: Reduced state of 16 friendly relations which might lead to ruin (8)

annotation.definitionNote: a descriptive phrase for a noun: a calamity is the thing which might lead to ruin

blocks.note: 16 is SAN DIEGO, in California, cut down to its abbreviation CAL
amity = friendly relations

annotation.surface: A warning that cooling relations with a city might end badly.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference sends you to 16 down, SAN DIEGO; its state, California, is shortened to CAL.
annotation.definitionFit: A calamity is a disaster, the sort of event that can bring ruin.

entries.clue: Vexatious occupation — wrong keeping it up? (3-2)

indicatorNotes.keeping: the wrong holds IT inside it

blocks.note: a sin is a wrong, split to hold IT
used as printed

annotation.surface: Asking whether a troublesome job is a mistake to keep doing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Occupation' looks like a job; here it is occupying a building in protest. 'Keeping it up' also nods to protesters keeping the sit-in going.
annotation.definitionFit: A sit-in is a protest occupation, meant to vex those in charge.

entries.clue: Sky viewer with unearthly interest in golf is out playing (9)

indicatorNotes.playing: the letters are played about with, like a round of golf

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A stargazer who has lost interest in golf now that it is not being played.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Unearthly interest' sounds like obsession; it is literal, an interest in things from beyond Earth.
annotation.definitionFit: A ufologist studies UFOs, watching the sky for visitors from beyond Earth.

entries.clue: Bad language changing? (14)

blocks.note: the surface pushes swearing; the setter means 'bad' as a verdict on what follows
the language is being changed into another one, and badly: a botched translation

annotation.surface: Swearing that is becoming more or less acceptable.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bad language' suggests swearing; read it as a bad changing of language, a botched translation.
annotation.definitionFit: A mistranslation is a faulty change from one language into another.

entries.clue: Following urge, that woman rows back from statement in court (4,8)

blocks.note: her = that woman
rows (rhyming with cows) are noisy quarrels, dins
last letter of statement
used as printed
CT is the abbreviation for court

annotation.surface: A woman retracting what she said in the witness box, under pressure to conform.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rows back' looks like a phrase for retracting a statement; 'rows' goes alone as noisy quarrels, and 'back' works with 'from statement'.
annotation.definitionFit: Herd instinct is the urge to follow what everyone else does.

entries.clue: Tamper with car to miss social outing (9)

indicatorNotes.Tamper with: to tamper with something is to interfere with its workings, so the letters are meddled into a new order

blocks.note: anagram indicator
anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Sabotaging someone's car so they can't get to a party.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Social outing' looks like a trip out with friends; it is being put out of society.
annotation.definitionFit: Ostracism is exclusion from society, an outing in the sense of being shut out.

entries.clue: Echo before long coming round in loop (5)

blocks.note: Echo is E in the NATO alphabet
soon = before long

annotation.surface: A patient told they will soon regain consciousness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Before' looks like a placement word, but 'before long' is one phrase meaning SOON.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: of all the loops of rope, the noose is the one that tightens as it is pulled.

entries.clue: Battery charge you’d say result of mobile phone use? (6)

indicatorNotes.you’d say: speak the two words and hear the answer

blocks.note: a battery is a cell, a charge is a fee

annotation.surface: Wondering whether draining your phone battery is the price of using it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Battery charge' reads as the power in a phone, which fits the surface; it is two words, cell and fee.
annotation.definitionFit: A selfie is a photo taken of yourself on a mobile phone.

entries.clue: Oddball went and died after eccentric life (4-5)

indicatorNotes.after: D comes after the rearranged LIFE
indicatorNotes.eccentric: the letters of LIFE behave oddly

blocks.note: left = went away
anagram of LIFE
d. = died, as in family trees

annotation.surface: An obituary of an odd character who led a strange life.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a potted life story; 'oddball' is an adjective here.
annotation.definitionFit: Left-field means unconventional or odd; oddball as an adjective means the same.

entries.clue: Prevented from wobbling, small camellia stopped (8)

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
the tea plant is a camellia, Camellia sinensis
an engine that died stopped

annotation.surface: A little camellia bush staked so it stops wobbling.
annotation.walkthrough: Camellia is the garden shrub in the surface; the tea plant belongs to the same genus.
annotation.definitionFit: Steadied means held firm, prevented from wobbling.

entries.clue: Chilean author failing to finish drink completely (3,4,2)

indicatorNotes.failing to finish: the author's name loses its last letter

blocks.note: Isabel ALLENDE, Chilean novelist, without her final E
to sup is to drink

annotation.surface: A novelist who can't finish her drink.
annotation.walkthrough: Isabel Allende is the Chilean author of The House of the Spirits.
annotation.definitionFit: To beat someone all ends up is to beat them completely.

entries.clue: City that is defined by smooth travel (3,5)

indicatorNotes.defined by: that is sits bounded by the other two pieces, smooth on one side and travel on the other

blocks.note: to sand wood is to smooth it
i.e. = that is
go = travel

annotation.surface: A city known for its easy travel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Defined by' sounds like 'characterised by'; it means bounded by, the way a border defines an area.
annotation.definitionFit: A bare category for a proper noun: the Californian port near the Mexican border is one city among many.

entries.clue: Soldier recalled evergreen old lover (8)

indicatorNotes.recalled: called back, so the tree is turned round

blocks.note: a fir is an evergreen tree
leman is an archaic word for a lover

annotation.surface: A soldier remembering a lasting old flame.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Evergreen' reads as an adjective for a lasting love; it is the tree.
annotation.definitionFit: A rifleman is an infantry soldier armed with a rifle.

entries.clue: Typewriter’s roller behind back of ribbon with page in front (6)

indicatorNotes.back of: take the last letter of ribbon
indicatorNotes.in front: the page goes at the start

blocks.note: p = page
late = behind time
last letter of ribbon

annotation.surface: How to load a typewriter: ribbon at the back, paper at the front.
annotation.walkthrough: Ribbon, page and roller all belong to a typewriter, so the wordplay hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: The platen is the roller a typewriter's paper wraps around.

entries.clue: Attraction of a ring in your ear? (6)

indicatorNotes.in your ear: what arrives in your ear is sound, so the words count by how they are heard, not how they are written

blocks.note: a peal is a ring of bells

annotation.surface: Asking why an earring is attractive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A ring in your ear' pictures an earring; the ring is a peal of bells.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something with appeal draws people in, as sex appeal or box-office appeal does.

entries.clue: Very boring article crammed with endless sport (5)

indicatorNotes.crammed with: the tool is stuffed with the sport
indicatorNotes.endless: the sport loses its last letter

blocks.note: an awl is a tool for boring holes, split to take FU
FUN without its last letter

annotation.surface: A dull item packed with half-finished games.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very boring' reads as one phrase, extremely dull; 'Very' is the definition and 'boring article' is the tool.
annotation.definitionFit: Awful can mean very, as in informal 'awful nice'.

entries.clue: On reversing, chunk taken from integral bumper (5)

indicatorNotes.chunk taken from: the answer is a piece of the next word

blocks.note: the end of integral holds the answer backwards

annotation.surface: A car bumper that loses a chunk when reversing.
annotation.walkthrough: Reversing and bumper belong to cars; 'bumper' is an adjective meaning large, as in a bumper crop.
annotation.definitionFit: Bumper means unusually large, as in a bumper harvest.

entries.clue: One supported man in court getting fine dropped for parking (9)

indicatorNotes.dropped for: F is dropped and P goes in its place

blocks.note: the man in the dock
f = fine, as on pencils
P = parking, on road signs

annotation.surface: A defendant whose fine is let off in exchange for a parking penalty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One supported man' looks like a phrase; 'One supported' ends the definition, and 'man in court' is the defendant.
annotation.definitionFit: A dependant is someone financially supported by another.

entries.clue: Where large dam was built almost entirely with spades once (2,3)

indicatorNotes.almost entirely: almost the entire word means nearly all of it, so the last letter is left off

blocks.clueFragment: Where large dam was built almost entirely
blocks.note: ASWAN, site of the Egyptian High Dam, without its last letter
S = spades, in card games

annotation.surface: A huge dam built almost entirely by hand with spades long ago.
annotation.walkthrough: The Aswan High Dam is on the Nile in Egypt. 'Once' looks like it belongs with the spades; it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: As was means formerly, as in 'Mrs Smith, Miss Jones as was'.

entries.clue: Man of Grieg’s genre who jazzed? (6,8)

annotation.definition: Man of Grieg’s genre who jazzed?

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 14 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A composer in Grieg's classical line who took up jazz.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: Gershwin wrote concert music in the classical tradition and brought jazz into it, in Rhapsody in Blue.
annotation.definitionFit: Gershwin was a classical-style composer who blended in jazz.

entries.clue: Eg chisel on front of shelf also going far right (4,4)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, one thing sitting on another comes straight after it, so 'also' follows the shortened shelf
indicatorNotes.going far right: the front letter of LEDGE moves to the far right end

blocks.note: LEDGE, a shelf, without its front letter
too = also
the L of LEDGE, moved to the end

annotation.surface: A chisel left on the front of a shelf, sliding off to the right.
annotation.walkthrough: The shelf is a LEDGE; its first letter travels to the far right, and TOO slots in before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by 'Eg': chisels, planes and axes are all tools with a cutting edge.

entries.clue: Take as given the cause of sub-postmistresses’ convictions? (5)

blocks.note: they worked for the Post Office, PO, with its possessive S
the computer system, information technology, that caused the convictions
surface only: says what IT caused, and the '?' flags the playful parse

annotation.surface: Assuming you know why sub-postmistresses were convicted.
annotation.walkthrough: In the Post Office Horizon scandal, faulty IT led to hundreds of British sub-postmasters being wrongly convicted of theft.
annotation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward as given, as a basis for argument.
